title: Operator Scenario Marketplace and Mentorship Program
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:

This page defines the Operator Scenario Marketplace (the marketplace) — an internal catalog and CI-validated registry of synthetic incident scenarios — and the paired Operator Mentorship Program designed to accelerate operator proficiency across the platform operator population. The goal is to make production-like incident practice repeatable, discoverable, and measurable, and to fold mentorship into regular operational training.

Why we need this:
- Operators encounter a wide range of inference-specific faults (prefix cache corruption, model-variant misrouting, cross-tenant token spikes, GPU thermal preemption). Ad-hoc drills leave knowledge gaps and are hard to audit.
- A centralized scenario registry + mentorship pairing increases reuse, shortens ramp time for new operators, and reduces mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to recover (MTTR).

Goals and success criteria:
- Provide a catalog of >= 60 vetted scenarios covering: cache, routing, model-swap, thermal/spot preemption, neighbor-tenant noisy behavior, and telemetry drift by Q3 2025.
- Each scenario has an owner, test manifest, acceptance criteria, and postmortem template.
- Mentorship pairs 1 senior operator to 2 new/junior operators; after 3 months, juniors should show a 25% reduction in MTTA on synthetic incidents.
- Track scenario usage and learning outcomes in a dashboard (see "Metrics and dashboard" section).

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: operator-facing simulation manifests, runbook snippets, playbooks for safe execution in a sandbox, and mentorship curriculum.
- Out-of-scope: production-changing automation (chaos that runs directly against production without a gate), vendor-managed training, and external customer-facing exercises.

Definitions:
- Scenario: A reproducible, parameterized incident simulation manifest (YAML) that can be executed in a sandbox or synthetic tenant.
- Marketplace: The git-backed registry and UI listing scenarios with metadata, tags, and test results.
- Simulation Owner: Person who vets and maintains a scenario.
- Mentor: Senior operator assigned to paired learning sessions.

Operator Scenario Manifest (required fields)
(Example manifest used by the CI validator and scenario runner)

---
name: prefix-cache-shard-corruption-v2
owner: eng-platform/operators-team
impact_area: runtime-kv-cache
severity: medium
description: "Simulate stale/incorrect KV prefix cache entries causing hallucinations and elevated token latency for a synthetic tenant."
environment: sandbox
prereqs:
  - synthetic-tenant: tenant-sim-014
  - model: redwood-vicuna-13b-quantized
steps:
  - action: seed-kv-shard
    params:
      key-prefix: "/user/sim/"
      corrupt-rate: 0.08
  - action: launch-load
    params:
      rps: 12
      profile: long-tail-1024
acceptance_criteria:
  - alert: kv-cache-error-rate < 500 per hour generated by simulation runner
  - slo_check: 95th_token_latency_delta > 25% from baseline
rollback_steps:
  - action: flush-kv-shard
  - action: revert-tenant-routing
observability_links:
  - /dashboards/eng-platform/runtime-prefix-cache-health
  - /dashboards/eng-platform/simulated-tenant-latency-traces
---

Scenario tagging taxonomy (required tags):
- impact_area: runtime-kv-cache | scheduling | routing | model-swap | network | infra-thermal | telemetry
- mode: sandbox | blue-green | shadow
- severity: low | medium | high | critical

Marketplace process and governance:
1) Submit a scenario MR to the marketplace repo (repo: github.com/redwood/platform-simulations). Include the manifest YAML, description, owner, expected telemetry signals, and a short runbook snippet.
2) CI validation runs static checks: required fields, safe-environment flag, presence of rollback steps, and test harness smoke-run in a simulated environment.
3) Two reviewers must approve: a runtime SME and an operator mentor.
4) Merge creates an entry in the marketplace UI and schedules the scenario for the quarterly validation run.

Safe execution guidelines:
- All scenarios must run in a sandbox tenant or a dedicated simulation cohort; no scenario may target production without an explicit multi-party approval and a written runbook that includes backout windows.
- Simulation noise must be rate-limited. Example: rps <= 20 for synthetic tenants; model-swap tests must be throttled to < 0.5% of model-serving capacity per region.
- Observability hooks (spans, traces, synthetic user tokens) must be labeled with tags scenario_id and sim_owner to avoid confusion with real incidents.

Mentorship Program overview:
- Pairing model: 1:2 senior-to-junior for a minimum 12-week pairing window. New hires and rotated engineers are prioritized.
- Commitments per mentor pair: two 90-minute scenario walkthroughs per week for first 4 weeks, then one guided drill per week for the following 8 weeks.
- Curriculum: week-by-week checklist covering foundational telemetry, top 10 infra faults, incident comms, SLO triage, and postmortem writing.

Mentorship session template:
- Pre-read: scenario manifest and baseline dashboard links (10m)
- Walkthrough: mentor talks through likely root causes, detection signals, and runbook steps (30m)
- Live run: junior executes the scenario in sandbox while mentor observes (30–45m)
- Debrief: write a short post-exercise note in the scenario entry and update the runbook snippet if gaps found (15m)

Post-exercise obligations:
- The simulation owner files a two-paragraph postmortem in the scenario entry and assigns any runbook bugs to the runbook backlog.
- Mentor and junior complete a short learning survey (3 questions) which feeds the operator learning dashboard.

Metrics and dashboard (implementation notes):
- Fields to capture per-execution: scenario_id, owner, mentor, participants, start_time, end_time, MTTA_sim, MTTR_sim, alerts_fired, false_positives, SLO_delta, and survey_score.
- We will onboard a dedicated dashboard in Grafana: "Operator Learning & Scenario Usage" with panels for usage by team, scenario heatmap, average MTTR improvements week-over-week, and mentor engagement rate.
- Baseline targets: by month 3 of mentorship, average MTTA_sim <= 3 minutes, MTTR_sim <= 18 minutes for medium severity scenarios.

Quality gates and continuous improvement:
- Quarterly scenario review cycle: all scenarios older than 6 months are re-validated by the simulation owner and a runtime SME.
- Retired scenarios must include a reason and a migration plan if the underlying infra changes (e.g., quantization rollout or runtime kernel update).

Operator certification and badges:
- Completion of the mentorship program + passing a scenario capstone (execute a medium+ scenario solo with MTTR_sim <= target) results in a "Certified Platform Operator (Level 1)" badge recorded in the team wiki.
- Senior mentors can nominate juniors for Level 2 after demonstrated independent incident leadership across 5 distinct scenarios.

Roadmap (next 12 months):
- Q2 2025: Launch marketplace MVP with 20 scenarios, CI validator, and initial mentor cohort (10 mentors).
- Q3 2025: Integrate scenario execution telemetry into Grafana dashboard and add automated post-exercise survey.
- Q4 2025: Add scenario tagging by customer-impact footprint and enable cross-team scenario sharing.
- Q1 2026: Develop an automated scenario-scheduling service to seed weekly practice rotations for oncall teams.

- Marketplace repo: github.com/redwood/platform-simulations (README: how to add a scenario)
- Scenario runner CLI: tools/sim-runner (usage: sim-runner --manifest path/to/manifest.yaml --dry-run)

How to propose a scenario (quick steps):
1) Fork platform-simulations -> add YAML manifest + runbook snippet + observability links.
2) Open MR and add the label "scenario-proposal".
3) Request reviewers: @runtime-sme and @mentor-coordinator.
4) After merge, schedule the scenario for the next quarterly validation run via the marketplace UI.

Appendix A — Scenario review checklist (CI + reviewers)
- Manifest schema validated (all required fields present)
- Safe environment flag is true and run environment is sandbox by default
- Rollback steps exist and restore points are defined
- Observability links included (dashboards, logs, traces)
- Acceptance criteria are measurable and tied to telemetry metrics
- Owner and mentor assigned

Appendix B — Quick example sim-runner commands
- Dry run: sim-runner --manifest scenarios/prefix-cache-shard-corruption-v2.yaml --dry-run
- Execute in sandbox: sim-runner --manifest scenarios/prefix-cache-shard-corruption-v2.yaml --env sandbox --approve

Appendix C — Post-exercise note template (copy into scenario entry)
- Summary: one-line summary of what happened
- Key signals observed: metrics/alerts that were most useful
- Action items: runbook updates or monitoring alerts to tune
- Learning: what the junior learned and what mentor recommends

FAQ
Q: Who can be a mentor?
A: Any operator with two+ years on the platform or a successful completion of the senior mentor course (listed in the learning catalog).

Q: Can scenarios run against a customer tenant?
A: No. Scenarios must use synthetic tenants or dedicated simulation cohorts; exceptions require documented approvals from Security and SRE and are extremely rare.

Q: How do we measure the program ROI?
A: Primary signals: reduction in MTTA/MTTR on synthetic incidents, mentor engagement rate, scenario reuse, and reduced frequency of repeated human errors on similar incident classes in production.

Contact and next steps:
- If you want to be a simulation owner or mentor, complete this short interest form: /forms/operator-simulation-interest (internal).
- To contribute a scenario now, see the contribution guide in the marketplace repo README.
